entries.proposition: The clinical evaluation is four patients on open-label add-on treatment with no control group; cognition was reported by parents without a standardised instrument.
entries.snippet: the clinical observations are based on open‑label add‑on treatment without a control group. Third, the cognitive improvements reported by parents were not assessed using standardized neuropsychological instruments.

entries.proposition: The authors did not test the drug on the mutant channels, so the proposed genotype-response link is untested.
entries.snippet: First, we did not directly test the ability of gabapentin to activate each mutant channel in vitro, as would be required to establish a mechanistic link between genotype and drug response.

entries.proposition: The authors call their explanation for the one non-responder speculative and note the drug has other targets.
entries.snippet: However, we emphasize that this interpretation remains speculative, as we did not directly test gabapentin’s effect on these mutant channels.

entries.proposition: Seizure freedom was assessed by video-EEG before and after initiation because clinical observation of seizures was hard.
entries.snippet: Because seizure identification solely by clinical observation was challenging, video‑EEG recordings were performed before and after gabapentin initiation to evaluate its therapeutic effect

entries.proposition: Three patients had earlier seizure-free periods on a sodium-channel blocker that ended in relapse after about 6 to 7 months, so a remission of that length can occur without the studied drug.
entries.snippet: Three of the four patients responded to oxcarbazepine (OXC), with Patient 3 remaining seizure‑free for nearly three years, whereas Patients 2 and 4 experienced seizure relapse after approximately six months.
entries.anchor: Results, Clinical features and genetic results

entries.proposition: Patient 2 became seizure-free only after 1 year and 5 months of exposure and patient 4 within 3 months, each against a background of fluctuating earlier courses.
entries.snippet: became seizure‑free after 1 year and 5 months on a low dose

entries.proposition: Patient 1 did not respond on EEG or seizures, yet the parents reported improved auditory responsiveness and babbling; the authors note improved alertness in this patient too.
entries.snippet: However, the parents reported cognitive improvements (increased auditory responsiveness and babbling) after gabapentin initiation.

entries.proposition: Parent-reported cognitive gains were described in all four patients including the non-responder, while motor improvement was absent in the three seizure-free patients; the authors say the improvements were similar across patients.
entries.snippet: Nevertheless, the cognitive improvements for the four patients with gabapentin in the study were similar based on their parents’ observations.

entries.proposition: A dose increase in patient 4 gave no further progress, the only dose-response observation.
entries.snippet: but further dose increase to 20 mg/kg/d did not lead to additional significant progress

entries.proposition: The mixed loss-and-gain description of the S4 variant rests on the homomeric channel; with its physiological partner subunit the variant keeps large currents (344.9 against 421.4 pA/pF at plus 60 mV, P above 0.05).
entries.snippet: p.L200P co‑expressed with KCNQ3 retained much larger currents (344.9 ± 49.0 pA/pF vs. 421.4 ± 50.5 pA/pF at + 60 mV, P > 0.05, Fig. 2b)

entries.proposition: The sample is four patients carrying four different variants, three of them in the same segment, so no replicate exists for any variant class.
The authors conclude gabapentin may be considered as an add-on in KCNQ2-DEE, particularly severe loss-of-function S6 variants, while stating the evidence is hypothesis-generating.
entries.snippet: our study provides real‑world, hypothesis‑generating data on the use of gabapentin in KCNQ2‑DEE

entries.proposition: Fig 1d-e: the S4 variant L200P gives smaller currents than wild type below about 20 mV and larger above, with an activation midpoint shifted from about minus 12 to plus 21 mV; the three S6 variants give no current; Fig 2b: with KCNQ3 the L200P current curve lies below the wild-type curve at nearly all voltages, about 150 against 270 pA/pF at 0 mV.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 1d current density: WT rises to about 118 pA/pF at +60; L200P below WT at -20 mV (***) and 0 mV, crosses at about +15 mV, about 298 at +60 (**); A294V, F305del, F305I flat near 0. Fig 1e G/Gmax midpoint WT about -12 mV, L200P about +21 mV. Fig 2b heteromeric: WT+KCNQ3 about 270 at 0 mV and 420 at +60; L200P+KCNQ3 about 150 at 0 mV and 345 at +60; A294V+KCNQ3 about 50 at +60; F305del and F305I about 0.

entries.proposition: Fig 3: EEG panels are single epochs; after gabapentin, patient 1 still shows hypsarrhythmia in sleep and patient 4 still shows bilateral frontal sharp waves, spikes and spike-wave complexes in sleep; the figure carries no counts or time series.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Fig 3 eight EEG epochs: (a) patient 1 sleep hypsarrhythmia before and after gabapentin, awake limb elevation with tremor before, awake fast rhythm with sharp waves after lamotrigine; (b) patient 4 sleep multifocal sharp waves before, awake staring and immobility before, sleep bilateral frontal sharp waves spikes and spike-slow wave complexes after gabapentin.
